description: We were never very good at staying on Earth.
summary: Martian Map is a platform we developed to help plan rover routes and explore the Martian surface. One of the main difficulties in Mars exploration is finding routes that are safe to travel while still reaching locations worth investigating. To address this, we use Martian geospatial data, such as elevation, slope, and terrain characteristics, to analyze the surface and calculate least-cost routes based on selected parameters and safety limits. We also developed a Science Mode that considers the distribution of resources, including water (H₂O), iron (Fe), and silicon (Si), to help identify areas of scientific interest. Through the platform, users can select destinations, view proposed routes, and examine details such as elevation profiles, slope variations, route length, estimated travel time, and resource distribution. What makes Martian Map useful is that it considers both the conditions a rover must cross and the scientific value of the places it may reach. Instead of selecting a route based only on distance or terrain, users can evaluate different paths while keeping exploration objectives in mind. This can help make rover route planning more practical and better aligned with the goals of a mission.
details:
Martian Map was developed to investigate how geospatial analysis can improve rover route planning by accounting for both terrain conditions and scientific objectives. The platform processes multiple Martian geospatial datasets, including elevation, slope, temperature, wind, and radiation, to evaluate the characteristics of the surface along potential routes.

The routing system is based on a least-cost path approach. Using Python, we process the input datasets as raster layers, normalize their values, and combine selected parameters through adjustable weights to generate a cost surface. Safety constraints are incorporated to identify terrain that may be unsuitable for rover movement. The pathfinding algorithm then searches this surface for a route with the lowest accumulated cost between the selected coordinates. This approach allows route selection to reflect terrain conditions rather than relying solely on geographical distance.

A separate Science Mode incorporates spatial resource data, including water (H₂O), iron (Fe), and silicon (Si), into the exploration process. This allows users to examine the distribution of these resources and consider their scientific relevance when evaluating potential destinations and routes.

The backend was implemented using Python and Django, with NumPy, Rasterio, Pandas, SciPy, and scikit-image supporting numerical computation, raster processing, and pathfinding. The frontend uses Next.js, React, and TypeScript to provide interactive maps, destination selection, route visualization, and analytical profiles. Users can examine elevation changes, slope conditions, route length, estimated travel time, and resource distribution. Vehicle-related parameters are also considered in route planning.

Several factors guided our design, including terrain accessibility, rover safety, the influence of individual environmental variables, computational efficiency, and the scientific relevance of exploration sites. A central aspect of the project is the integration of terrain-based navigation with resource analysis, allowing route evaluation to account for both operational feasibility and potential scientific value.
